state.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Grants
state.sum: The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) provides grants through the It Pay$ to Plug In: New Jersey’s Electric Vehicle Workplace Charging Grant Program (Program) for EV charger installation.

state.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) and EV Charger Grant Program
state.sum: The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) administers the eMobility Grant Program, which provides funding to increase electric mobility solutions including carshare, rideshare, ride-hailing, fixed-route transit, microtransit, and e-mobility services for residents in underserved areas .

state.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) and EV Charger Rebate
state.sum: The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities’ (NJBPU) Charge Up New Jersey program offers point-of-sale rebates to New Jersey residents for the purchase or lease of a new light-duty EV. A rebate of $1,500 is available for eligible EVs with a manufacturer suggested retail price of up to $55,000.

state.title: Multifamily Housing (MFH) Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Grants
state.sum: The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities’ (NJBPU) MFH EV Charger Incentive Program offers grants to MFH owners of up to $4,000 for the purchase and installation of eligible, dual-port Level 2 EV chargers.

laws.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Policies for Residential Associations
laws.sum: Residential associations may not prohibit or restrict the installation or use of EV chargers in a homeowner’s designated parking space. Residential associations may put reasonable restrictions on EV chargers, but the policies may not significantly increase the cost of the EV charger or prohibit installation.

laws.title: Residential Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Installation Policies
laws.sum: A developer of a single-family residence that includes a designated parking space must offer to install an EV charger at the residence of the prospective owner unless the installation of the EV charger is already included in the sale of the unit.

laws.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Make-Ready Requirements for Multifamily Housing (MFH)
laws.sum: New or reconstructed MFH developments with five or more units must designate 15% of required off-street parking as EV make-ready parking spaces, in proportion to new or reconstructed MFH. Prior to occupancy, EV chargers must be installed in 5% of off-street parking.
